_README: Copy this to study.json, edit, and run:
Everything the build assumes about your images lives in this one file:
where they are, how they are named, which channel holds which dye, how the
grid is cut, and the exact wording counters read in English and German.
Point it at a different stain, a different tissue or a different depth
Every key is optional. Anything you leave out keeps its built-in default,
and command-line flags still override this file.
Keys ending _de are the German text. If one is missing the English is used,
_source: Folder holding the images, relative to the Sclera project folder.
_stacks: Which z-stacks to use. Each is <specimen>/<image stem>; the region folder is
found automatically. Files must be named '<image> _zNN.png', e.g.
_z_levels: Which slices to sample from every stack. Stacks here run z00..z19 at
5.263 um, so 5,9,13,17 spans about 26-89 um. Use a denser ladder near the
depth where counting starts to fail if that is the question.
_grid: How each field is divided. 8 columns x 8 rows = 64 squares.
_field_width_um: Physical width of one field, from calibration.yaml. Sets the micron scale.
_scheme: Which staining scheme below to build with.
_schemes: Add an entry here for a new stain. 'nuclei', 'dead' and 'live' name the RGB
channel each dye sits in; set the ones your stain has and leave the rest null.
Only a stain that labels EVERY cell (like Hoechst) can support a 'count the
total' task. With a stain that marks only a subset there is no denominator,
so offer the live/dead style task instead.
'layers' are the views a counter can switch between; the keys must be
'merged' plus whichever of nuclei/live/dead your channels define.
'modes' are the counting tasks offered on the start screen.

_comment: A worked example: DAPI nuclei in blue plus a propidium iodide dead
marker in red. Rename the key, drop the underscore, and set

layers.name: All nuclei
layers.hint: DAPI. Every spot is a nucleus - this is the TOTAL
layers.hint_de: DAPI. Jeder Fleck ist ein Zellkern - das ist die GESAMTZAHL

layers.name: Dead only
layers.hint: PI. A spot here on a nucleus means that nucleus is DEAD
layers.hint_de: PI. Ein Fleck hier auf einem Zellkern bedeutet: dieser Kern ist TOT

cells.label: Nuclei only
cells.prompt: Click every nucleus on the DAPI layer. Do not judge live or dead.
cells.prompt_de: Klicken Sie jeden Zellkern in der DAPI-Ansicht an. Ohne Beurteilung von lebend oder tot.

livedead.label: Live / dead
livedead.prompt: Click every nucleus. A nucleus with PI on it is dead; one without is live.
livedead.prompt_de: Klicken Sie jeden Zellkern an. Ein Kern mit PI ist tot, ein Kern ohne PI ist lebend.
